sources.title: Third-person self-talk facilitates emotion regulation without engaging cognitive control: Converging evidence from ERP and fMRI
sources.why_it_matters: Proved via converging human ERP and fMRI that switching inner speech from 'I' to one's own first name drops emotional brain reactivity within 1 second and reduces medial prefrontal + amygdala activity without taxing cognitive control.

sources.title: Self-talk as a regulatory mechanism: How you do it matters.
sources.journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
sources.why_it_matters: Demonstrated across 6 behavioral studies using the Trier Social Stress Test (5-minute speech with 2 minutes prep) that third-person name self-talk improves speech performance and cuts post-event rumination.

sources.title: Does Distanced Self-Talk Facilitate Emotion Regulation Across a Range of Emotionally Intense Experiences?
sources.why_it_matters: Verified that distanced third-person self-talk regulates high-intensity real-world anxiety without losing effectiveness when emotional intensity rises.

sources.title: Salivary cortisol as a biomarker in stress research
sources.why_it_matters: Established methodological standards and physiological bounds of Trier Social Stress Test stress biomarkers.

sources.title: The ‘Trier Social Stress Test’ – A Tool for Investigating Psychobiological Stress Responses in a Laboratory Setting
sources.why_it_matters: Original laboratory validation of the Trier Social Stress Test (impromptu speech + mental arithmetic before an evaluative panel) driving reliable 2-to-4-fold cortisol surges.

sources.title: When Asking “Why” Does Not Hurt Distinguishing Rumination From Reflective Processing of Negative Emotions
sources.why_it_matters: Foundational Psychological Science discovery showing self-distanced perspective-taking turns toxic rumination into calm reflective processing.
